intro: IBPS Clerk (Customer Service Associate) is a state-wise exam with a qualifying Preliminary exam and a merit-deciding Main exam; there is no interview. The notification names each test with its question count, marks and timing, but does not itemise a topic-wise syllabus.
note: The topic lists below are the conventional scope of IBPS Clerk papers mapped to this site's subjects; treat them as a study map and check the official notification for the final word. Structure per the CRP CSA-XVI notification (1 August 2026): Prelims is 100 questions for 100 marks in 60 minutes with a separate 20-minute timer per section (English Language 30 questions for 30 marks, Numerical Ability 35 for 35, Reasoning 35 for 35). Mains is 160 questions for 200 marks in 125 minutes with separately timed sections and weighted marking (General/Financial Awareness 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes, General English 40 for 40 in 35 minutes, Reasoning 40 for 60 in 35 minutes, Quantitative Aptitude 40 for 50 in 35 minutes; 1.5 marks per question in Reasoning, 1.25 in Awareness and Quant, 1.0 in English). One-fourth of the marks assigned to a question are deducted for each wrong answer. Recruitment is state-wise: you apply for one state/UT only.

sections.name: English Language (Prelims) / General English (Mains)
topics: Reading comprehension (passages with questions on main idea, inference and vocabulary in context)
Fill in the blanks (single and double)
Synonyms and antonyms, idioms and phrases
sections.tip: English is a flat 1 mark per question in both stages, but the Mains gives 40 questions in 35 minutes, so the section rewards steady reading speed rather than tricks.

sections.name: Numerical Ability (Prelims) / Quantitative Aptitude (Mains)
topics: Data interpretation: tables, bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, caselets and missing-data sets
Percentage, ratio and proportion, average and ages
Time and work, pipes and cisterns
Time, speed and distance, trains and boats
Arithmetic word problems on the above topics
sections.tip: The Prelims calls it Numerical Ability (35 questions for 35 marks in 20 minutes) and stays closer to school-level arithmetic; the Mains calls it Quantitative Aptitude (40 questions for 50 marks in 35 minutes, 1.25 per question) with a heavier data-interpretation share.

sections.name: Reasoning Ability
topics: Puzzles and seating arrangement (linear, circular, floor-based, scheduling, box and tabular)
Statement and conclusion, statement and assumption
sections.tip: The heaviest mains section: 40 questions for 60 marks in 35 minutes (1.5 per question). Puzzles and seating arrangements dominate recent papers, and the 20-minute Prelims timer leaves no room to get stuck on a single set.

sections.name: General / Financial Awareness
topics: Current affairs of roughly the last six months, weighted toward finance and the economy
RBI circulars, policy and payment systems
sections.tip: Mains only: 40 questions for 50 marks in just 20 minutes (1.25 per question), so it is a pure recall sprint over current affairs, banking and financial awareness, RBI functions and government schemes.

sections.name: Computer Knowledge (eligibility requirement, no separate mains test)
sections.tip: The revised CRP CSA-XVI mains has no separate computer section, but computer literacy is an eligibility requirement (a certificate or diploma in computer operations or language, or Computer/IT as a subject in school or college), and digital-banking awareness helps in the Awareness section.
